title: Case: Customer with a cracked planter asks where her replacement is
context: A large ceramic planter (order TG-9363, shipment DL-3721) arrived cracked on 2026-06-04. Heronwick's Damage intake team runs the claim; Replacement authorisations decides replacements once intake is complete.
initial_request: I am writing by email because the portal is plainly a black hole. It is now six days since I reported a planter that arrived in two pieces, more or less. I sent photographs the same afternoon. Since then I have had: an automatic reply, a reminder that I have unread messages which turn out to be adverts, an email about replacing my pots which turned out to be an advert for more planters, and a refund of four pounds for some twine, which is not what I asked about. What I have not had is a single sentence from a human being about the planter. I have the broken one sitting in its box in my hallway taking up room. I sent you everything you could possibly need on day one. So where is my replacement, and when is someone coming for this one? If I do not hear by Friday I will be disputing the charge with my bank.

expected.reference_message: Dear Ms Dunmore, I am sorry you have had no proper reply since the 4th. Your three photos of the planter were received and accepted, and damage claim DC-8501 is open for shipment DL-3721. One thing is still missing that nobody asked you for: a photo of the outer box showing the shipping label, so the carrier can match the carton. Heronwick's Damage intake team needs it by 2026-06-12 or the claim closes automatically, so please keep the box and send that photo as soon as you can, by reply to this email. Once intake is complete, the decision on a replacement is made by Heronwick's Replacement authorisations team; I cannot confirm that or a collection of the damaged planter for them, but I will pass your photo on the moment it arrives and tell you what they decide. Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
